submission.justification: Radiator-R3 at 3.5 cm thickness is recommended as it provides the best balance of performance and reliability. The simulation shows 3.754 sigma pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c, which comfortably exceeds the 3.5 sigma hard requirement. Most critically, R3 features a hydrophobic treatment specifically designed to protect against humidity-induced transparency loss, which is essential since the radiator cannot be replaced during the 10-year run. While Radiator-R1 offers higher separation performance (up to 4.7 sigma), it lacks hydrophobic protection and as a porous radiator would likely fail the transparency loss requirement after long-term humidity exposure. Radiator-R2 does not meet the separation requirement at any thickness. The 3.5 cm thickness for R3 provides optimal separation performance within the allowed range, with performance declining at both thinner and thicker values.

requirements.requirement: Pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c must be at least 3.5 sigma
requirements.evidence: Simulation shows 3.754 sigma separation for Radiator-R3 at 3.5 cm thickness, exceeding the 3.5 sigma requirement.

requirements.requirement: Transparency loss after 10-year humidity ageing test must not exceed 10%
requirements.evidence: Radiator-R3 is specifically described as having hydrophobic treatment, designed to resist humidity-induced degradation. This distinguishes it from R1 (porous without treatment) and addresses the hard requirement for long-term stability.
Recommended thickness of 3.5 cm is within the specified range of 1-6 cm.

requirements.requirement: Radiator must be one of three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Radiator-R3 is one of the three candidates specified in candidate_specs.md.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c
requirements.evidence: Among radiators that meet all hard constraints, R3 at 3.5 cm provides 3.754 sigma separation. While R1 offers higher separation, it likely fails the transparency loss requirement due to lack of hydrophobic treatment.
